title: Hybrid tile allocator with eviction-aware KV stitching and scratch pool
author: Aman Patel
release_notes: Reduced peak GPU working set by up to ~18% for long-context workloads and reduced 99th-percentile latency through lower fragmentation and smarter KV eviction. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Context and motivation: Certain long-context and multi-concurrent-session workloads were triggering large transient scratch and KV allocations causing fragmentation and out-of-memory (OOM) spikes on high-utilization Dedicated nodes. Existing arena allocators favored large contiguous slabs which reduced fragmentation for some workloads but left many small-lived activation spikes unhandled, and the KV cache eviction was ignorant of scratch tile locality leading to redundant re-materialization costs. This PR implements a hybrid tile-based scratch allocator plus an eviction-aware KV stitching layer and accompanying scheduling hints to reduce peak GPU workspace and improve steady-state latency.

High-level solution summary: 1) Hybrid tile allocator: split the scratch arena into configurable fixed-size tiles (default 64KB) and a small slab pool for large contiguous requests. Tile allocations are compacted into bitmaps to reduce metadata overhead and allow O(1) free/alloc. Support deferred zeroing for tiles to avoid eager memset on reuse. 2) Eviction-aware KV stitching: when the KV cache evicts a chunk, we record tile-locality hints so subsequent re-materialization prefers reusing nearby tiles or the small-slab pool, lowering cross-allocation churn. A lightweight stitch table maps activation ranges -> tile extents for reattachment without full re-copy in many hot paths. 3) Scheduler integration: the request scheduler obtains a tile footprint estimate per request (derived from model and sequence length) and schedules compatible batches to colocate allocations, minimizing fragmentation. The scheduler will prefer draining small-tile-heavy queues to the slab pool when fragmentation exceeds thresholds. 4) Continuous batching adjustments: batching now respects tile boundaries when forming micro-batches to avoid requests forcing expensive slab allocations mid-batch. 5) Telemetry and heuristics: new metrics exposing tile utilization, tile-fragmentation score, KV-stitch hit/miss counters, and a new SLO guard that triggers conservative slab reservations under high tile fragmentation.

Files changed (high level): runtime/scratch/tile_allocator.h, runtime/scratch/tile_allocator.cpp, runtime/scratch/slab_pool.cpp, runtime/kv/eviction_stitch.cpp, runtime/kv/eviction_stitch.h, scheduler/placement.h, scheduler/placement.cc, scheduler/batching_policy.cc, bench/bench_tile_allocator.cc, tests/integration/kv_stitch_smoke.cc, docs/ops/tuning/tile_allocator.md, ci/workflows/allocator-smoke.yml.

Commits summary: - feat(scratch): add basic tile allocator, bitmap free lists, deferred zeroing (initial implementation) - feat(kv): add stitch table, tile locality hints and lightweight persistence-friendly metadata - feat(scheduler): expose tile footprint API and batch formation guard - perf(bench): microbench harness and end-to-end benchmark comparing baseline vs hybrid allocator - fix(tests): update integration mocks and unit tests to use new allocator primitives - ci: add allocator smoke matrix to run on GPU runners

Benchmarks and results: microbench results on p4d.24xlarge-like nodes (mixed sequences and batching patterns) show median GPU working set reduction of 9-18% depending on model topology and sequence distribution. 99th-percentile tail latency improved by 6-12% in high-concurrency scenarios due to fewer OOM-driven rescues and lower re-materialization cost. Throughput held constant or improved slightly (+1-4%) because allocation path improvements reduced scheduling stalls. Tile-fragmentation metric showed a ~40% reduction versus slab-only baseline under synthetic adversarial workloads.

Compatibility and config: Feature gated behind runtime flag tile_allocator.enabled and tuning knobs tile_size, slab_threshold_pct, and kv_stitch_enabled. Defaults are conservative and should be safe for existing deployments. No API surface changes for customers; internal config values are exposed to Dedicated/private operators in the Console.

Review conversation (abridged): - Liam Chen: "This looks promising; please add a safety valve when tile bitmap becomes highly fragmented to avoid pathological OOMs." -> Response (Aman): "Added slab reservation heuristic and SLO guard + tests." - Sofia Ruiz: "Can we avoid atomic contention on the bitmap in high concurrency?" -> Response: "Used per-thread allocation caches and batched bitmap commits; added microbench showing no throughput regression." - Morgan Li: "Add telemetry and ops docs for tuning tile_size vs model footprints." -> Response: "Added docs/ops/tuning/tile_allocator.md and dashboards for tile utilization." - Code review requested minor naming and style changes; they were addressed in follow-up commits.

CI and rollout story: First CI run failed lint (naming) and a flaky unit test in integration; those were fixed in subsequent commits. Full CI (unit + bench smoke matrix + allocator smoke workflow) passed on 2024-11-19. Feature was rolled out to internal canary cluster (Dedicated alpha pool) for a week, observed no regressions and the expected working set reductions; incrementally enabled via runtime flag and promoting to production after approval.

Risks and mitigations: - Risk: tile size misconfiguration could increase slab usage -> mitigation: conservative default, autosizing telemetry, and admin alerting when slab_threshold_pct exceeded. - Risk: KV-stitch table could add metadata overhead -> mitigation: stitch table is LRU bounded and stored in pinned host memory; eviction metrics included. - Risk: race on reattachment path under preemption -> mitigation: added lightweight epoch checks and unit tests simulating preemption.

Merge and post-merge: Squash-merged after approvals on 2024-11-20. Post-merge tasks: add operator-facing runbook entry, schedule perf regression watch for 1 week, and follow-up ticket ENG-2053 to explore hardware-specific tile_size heuristics for A100 vs H100.

Checklist: - [x] Unit & integration tests updated - [x] Benchmarks added - [x] Docs/ops guidance included - [x] CI passes (after fixes) - [x] Backward compatible by default

References: ENG-1984 (investigation), ENG-2027 (scheduler integration), SUP-562 (customer incident prompting priority).

Notes for reviewers: focus on concurrency invariants in tile allocator and correctness of stitch reattachment logic. The allocator code is intentionally small and well-commented to ease audit.
